items.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01
items.q: He had Otto, a fellow on saxophone, and he was in need of saxophone players

ctx.x: You went on to New York band with them? With that section.

And on the percussion we had on piano, Louis Russell and Paul Barbaran on drums. But the band didn't have any success. We stayed there and we worked at the Savoy Ballroom. We had no more than about two weeks and whatever came up, King Oliver came out. He didn't seem, he could get enough money. So he had offered to go to the cotton club and that was his great mistake. He wouldn't accept it. And that was King Oliver's downfall. Because he didn't think there was enough money in it and he wouldn't accept it. So Duke…
That's when Barney went with him.
